title: Runtime ABI stabilization and phased deprecation windows
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Purpose:
Establish a concrete, runtime-focused semantic versioning policy that treats the runtime binary & public on-disk/IPC/ABI contracts as first-class artifacts. This ticket defines: ABI stability rules, soft-deprecation windows, LTS channel guarantees, rollout gate criteria, and the upgrade tooling we will ship to make non-breaking migrations reliable and observable.

Scope (what this policy covers):
- Public RPC/gRPC API surface used by SDKs and internal agents (request/response schemas, headers, status codes).
- Runtime binary ABI that consumers rely on for plugin extensions and customer-managed private deployments (on-disk cache formats, serialized KV cache files, planner state snapshots).
- Network contract (TLS handshake/versioning compatibility, accepted protocol versions).
- Feature flags and config knobs that change runtime behavior (e.g., KV cache eviction semantics, batching strategy signals).
- Schema evolution for structured output and function-calling metadata.

Core rules (proposed):
1) Semver baseline: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH where MAJOR implies an incompatible change to any of the scoped contracts above that cannot be mitigated by shims. MINOR may introduce new fields or opt-in behaviors and can include "soft" deprecations with a published migration path. PATCH is backwards-compatible bug fixes only.
2) ABI stability banding: classify contracts into three bands with documented guarantees:
   - Band A (stable runtime contract): guaranteed across all MINOR/PATCH releases within an LTS MAJOR for at least 18 months or until the next LTS MAJOR. Examples: public REST/gRPC endpoints, canonical SDK types, de/serialization format for KV cache.
   - Band B (relaxed compatibility): allowed controlled additive changes in MINOR releases, must include runtime warning headers and compatibility score >= 0.9 in smoke-tests. Examples: telemetry enrichment fields, non-critical config flags.
   - Band C (experimental): no stability guarantee; may change without incrementing MAJOR. Must be behind explicit feature flag.
3) Soft-deprecation windows: for any deprecation that is not a MAJOR-breaking change we will publish a deprecation announcement and observe a minimum 90-day window before removal. For LTS customers we provide a 180-day extended window and a backport option on request.
4) Breaking-change workflow: any change that would increment MAJOR must go through the Breaking Change RFC + Steering review + Compatibility Impact Assessment (telemetry + smoke-run). If approved, the change is scheduled for the next MAJOR release and accompanied by: compatibility shims when feasible, migration tooling, and a documented rollback plan.

Rollout gates and telemetry signals:
- Canary -> Ramp -> Global. Canonical canary: 1% traffic, 24h synthetic runbook. Ramp phases: 5%, 25%, 60% with at least one full infer traffic pattern pass at each stage.
- Automated tests at each gate: unit compat suite, cross-version KV cache replay, SDK contract fuzzing, downstream integration smoke tests.
- Gate failure criteria (example thresholds):
   - Errors increased > 0.5% absolute or > 3x baseline on critical endpoints
   - P99 latency regression > 20% or > 50ms absolute (whichever stricter)
   - Compatibility score drop below 0.95 for Band A endpoints
- Telemetry signals to publish: deprecation header exposures, client library warnings, number of distinct customers using deprecated features, failed migration attempts.

Upgrade tooling and developer ergonomics:
- migration-assistant CLI: a tool to scan a customer's usage (prompts, SDK versions, persisted cache files) and produce a per-customer migration plan with estimated token-cost/regression risk and required changes.
- compatibility-checker CI job: runs cross-version compatibility matrix tests automatically for PRs touching runtime contracts. Produces a machine-readable compatibility report and a human summary.
- shim-generator: where feasible generate compatibility shims at build-time that translate old serialized formats to new ones for an automated fallback during ramp. Shims must be opt-in and gated by a flag; they should be marked Band-specific and removed only after deprecation window.
- deprecation headers: add 'X-Redwood-Deprecation' and structured 'X-Redwood-Deprecation-Detail' (JSON blob as string) to responses so SDKs and customers can detect impending removals programmatically.

Operational requirements before shipping change:
- Written compatibility impact assessment attached to the PR (link to doc).
- Automated cross-version tests green for all Band A endpoints across all supported LTS MAJOR versions.
- Migration assistant preview runs on a non-production snapshot for at least 3 impacted customers (internal or partner customers) when feasible.
- Rollout runbook with explicit rollback steps and contact list.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Formal policy document (this ticket -> final doc) to be published in Confluence and linked in release notes.
- compatibility-checker CI pipeline (prototype integration).
- migration-assistant CLI skeleton and a roadmap for integration with console.
- Example deprecation headers implementation on runtime-1.20 branch and a demo PR linking to SDK warning behavior.

Open questions / decisions needed by 2025-03-10:
- Exact deprecation window length for MINOR non-LTS customers (proposal: 90 days); confirm.
- Band assignment owner: who decides banding for new contracts? (proposal: API/Platform PM + Runtime Tech Lead).
- Policy for on-disk cache major-version compatibility: allow automatic conversion shims or require manual migration?

References and artifacts:
- Draft RFC: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/RUNTIME-ABI-RFC (placeholder link)
- Prototype PR for deprecation headers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1242
- Example migration-assistant spike: drive.google.com/file/d/1-example-spike

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers with long-lived on-disk caches break during upgrades. Mitigation: require conversion shim or offline migration tool and detect via compatibility-checker.
- Risk: Too conservative policy slows innovation. Mitigation: Band C experimental channel and explicit opt-in flags for rapid iteration.

Success criteria (by release-1.20):
- Published policy doc and Confluence page with band definitions.
- compatibility-checker runs on PRs and blocks merges with severe regressions.
- migration-assistant MVP can produce at least one automated migration plan for partner snapshot data.
